text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm proposing we simplify the SDK pagination surface into two clear patterns: an explicit FetchPage(token, opts) primitive and a StreamPages() async/iterator-style helper that wraps FetchPage. Rationale: fewer moving parts in transport layer and clearer retry semantics.

josh: +1 on clarity. Can you call out how retries work for StreamPages vs FetchPage?

maria: Good call. FetchPage should be the source of truth for transport behavior: callers get granular control (per-call timeouts, idempotency flag). StreamPages will implement best-effort retries for transient failures only when the last operation is idempotent and will expose a hook for user-supplied retry policy.

kai: How do we express idempotency in language surfaces? For Go I like explicit options on the call, for TS maybe an overloaded call, Python could use a param or context manager.

maria: Exactly — keep the shapes idiomatic: Go: FetchPage(ctx, req, opts...), TS: fetchPage(req, {idempotent: true}), Python: fetch_page(req, idempotent=True) or via a Request object. Important: names consistent across SDKs.

ben: What about streaming backpressure and partial-page failures? If a page has N items and one item parsing fails, we should surface a page-level error and not try to resume mid-page. StreamPages can emit a partial result + error event but default should be fail-fast so callers don't get inconsistent reads.

maria: Agree. We'll document "atomic page" contract: a page is delivered whole or the call fails. For large pages recommend smaller page_size or server-side chunking.

josh: Transport choices: do we standardize on a single HTTP+JSON fetch for all SDKs, or keep gRPC for Go and HTTP for TS/Python? Keeping one simplifies retries/trace but gRPC gives better streaming semantics.

kai: I'd vote lib-level abstraction: a Transport interface with two capabilities: unary fetch (FetchPage) and server-stream (optional). Default implementations: HTTP/JSON for cross-lang parity; gRPC-backed transport enabled for Go where available. That keeps surface stable while allowing optimized transports.

maria: Exactly. Transport abstraction prevents surface churn. We'll mark server-stream as experimental capability and fallback to unary when not present.

ben: Rollout plan? We need backwards compatibility: existing SDKs expose an iterator and a page token API. How to migrate without breaking?

maria: Migration plan: 1) Add FetchPage while keeping existing iterator. 2) Deprecate old iterator in favor of StreamPages after a 3-month overlap. 3) Provide a shim that maps old iterator to StreamPages (best-effort) to minimize user friction.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: New proposal posted: PR #4231 linking SDK shapes and transport interface. CI will run compatibility checks on all language SDKs.

josh: One more concern: latency vs cost. If StreamPages does aggressive retries, small transient errors could multiply requests. We need a default retry budget and telemetry hooks.

maria: We'll add default retry budget and per-route metrics (retry_count, retry_budget_exhausted). Owners can tune defaults per customer profile.

kai: For ergonomics: in TypeScript provide both async iterable and a callback-style stream. For Python, both generator and async generator. Go should keep a channel-based helper.

ben: thumbs up. Document examples: `for await (const page of client.streamPages(req))` and `resp = client.fetchPage(req, {idempotent: true})`.

maria: I'll draft an RFC addendum with sample code for all three languages and a compatibility timeline. Posting in PR by EOD. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
